data.name: FKBP12
data.description: Rapamycin's docking protein. Rapamycin first binds FKBP12; only the FKBP12-rapamycin pair can grab mTOR. This is why rapamycin is an 'allosteric' (indirect) inhibitor - it works through a chaperone, not by blocking the active site.
data.description_beginner: The 'docking protein' rapamycin needs to work. Rapamycin first grabs onto this protein, and only that combined pair can then latch onto and block mTOR - which is why rapamycin is called an indirect ('allosteric') inhibitor rather than one that blocks mTOR's active site directly.

reading_levels.student: Prolyl isomerase that forms the drug-receptor complex with rapamycin.
reading_levels.research: FKBP1A. Rapamycin has essentially no activity against mTOR without it, which is why FKBP12 expression sets rapalog sensitivity.

studies.title: Structure of the FKBP12-rapamycin complex interacting with the binding domain of human FRAP
studies.authors: Choi J; Chen J; Schreiber SL; Clardy J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The crystal structure that showed HOW rapamycin works at the atomic level: one rapamycin molecule glues two proteins together - FKBP12 and mTOR's FRB domain - by plugging into two hydrophobic pockets at once. A textbook example of a small molecule acting as 'molecular glue' to force protein dimerization.

studies.title: mTOR kinase structure, mechanism and regulation
studies.authors: Yang H; Rudge DG; Koos JD; Vaidialingam B; Yang HJ; Pavletich NP

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Solved the crystal structure of the mTOR kinase itself. Revealed why the active site is so hard to reach - it sits in a deep recess guarded by the FRB domain, which acts as a 'gatekeeper' letting substrates in. This structure explains at the atomic level exactly how FKBP12-rapamycin blocks access, and why activating cancer mutations cluster where they do.

studies.title: Structure of the human mTOR complex I and its implications for rapamycin inhibition
studies.authors: Yip CK; Murata K; Walz T; Sabatini DM; Kang SA

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human mTORC1 purified from HEK-293T cells stably expressing FLAG-raptor; negative-stain and cryo-EM (26 A); antibody labelling; in vitro kinase assays on S6K1 and 4E-BP1 with FKBP12-rapamycin or Torin1
studies.finding: The authors purified intact, active human mTORC1 and solved its shape by cryo-electron microscopy at about 26 angstrom resolution. The complex is an obligate dimer with a rhomboid outline and a central cavity, held together by interlocking contacts between mTOR and Raptor; antibody labelling placed mLST8 at the outer 'feet' and PRAS40 next to Raptor. Exposing purified mTORC1 to FKBP12-rapamycin first added a bound density in about 10% of particles, then broke the complex apart, with virtually no intact particles left after one hour, while the ATP-competitive inhibitor Torin1 left it intact. In matching kinase assays, FKBP12-rapamycin blocked S6K1 phosphorylation quickly but 4E-BP1 phosphorylation only after at least 60 minutes, and Raptor-free mTOR still phosphorylated S6K1 (rapamycin-sensitively) but not 4E-BP1. The authors proposed that rapamycin inhibits the two substrates by different mechanisms. Boundary: Purified protein and low-resolution EM; the authors note that in cells rapamycin neither fully blocks 4E-BP1 phosphorylation nor dismantles mTORC1, so the disassembly model is an in vitro result.

relations.mechanism: Only when it is carrying rapamycin, FKBP12 docks on the FRB domain next to mTOR's active site. The FKBP12-rapamycin complex, not FKBP12 alone, is what blocks access for some substrates but not all; FKBP12 without the drug does not inhibit mTORC1. The inhibitory arrow is drawn from rapamycin (RAPA-MTORC1).
relations.mechanism_beginner: Only when it carries rapamycin does FKBP12 dock on mTORC1; the pair then blocks some, but not all, of what mTORC1 does. FKBP12 on its own does nothing to mTORC1.
relations.boundary: Biochemical and structural work on rat and bovine brain extracts, rodent and T cells, and a cryo-EM structure of human mTORC1. It defines how the drug-bound complex docks. FKBP12 alone does not inhibit mTORC1, and effects in whole animals are carried by the rapamycin edges, not this one.

relations.mechanism: Rapamycin is not an ordinary inhibitor: it first binds the small protein FKBP12, and only the two-part complex is the real drug.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Rapamycin doesn't work alone – it first has to team up with a helper protein called FKBP12.
relations.boundary: X-ray crystallography and in vitro work on bovine, rat and mouse material (CHO1996, BRO1994, SAB1995). Describes drug binding in purified systems; it says nothing about dose or effect in patients.
relations.note: The molecular-glue concept - genuinely surprising to newcomers.
